name: Taurine cattle domestication in the upper Euphrates valley
summary: Cattle bones from early farming villages on the upper Euphrates are argued to show the first domestic cattle, the contested starting point of taurine herds across Eurasia and Africa.
description: At Dja'de al-Mughara on the Syrian Euphrates, dated to the early Pre-Pottery Neolithic B, Helmer argues from a small reduction in the size of male cattle that villagers were already breeding aurochs as domestic cattle. A 2021 review calls that change small and contested, and places the earliest large reduction in body size on the Euphrates at Mezraa-Teleilat in the early to mid eighth millennium BC. The same review reports a genetic argument that as few as 80 female aurochs, in one or two villages such as Dja'de, founded taurine cattle.

impact.note: Taurine cattle descended from south-west Asian founders came to be kept by most farming societies of Eurasia and Africa and later the Americas; they added a new capability, a large herd animal for meat, milk and work, and dairying and ox traction grew from it. Reach rests on the general view that these herds descend from this region, which the review reports but qualifies.

date.label: early PPNB, 8500–8000 cal BCE
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: A review reports Helmer's argument that cattle at Dja'de al-Mughara, a site of the early PPNB (8500–8000 calibrated BC in the review's Table 1), are the first to show domestic form; the review itself regards the size change as small and contested.

evidence.supports: Dramatic changes in human cattle relationships are reflected at the site of Dja’de al-Mughara dating to the early PPNB ( EPPNB ), where Helmer argues morphologically domestic cattle are evident for the first time

date.label: middle PPNB, early to mid 8th millennium BCE
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: The review's own measurements put the earliest large reduction in cattle body size in the Euphrates region at Mezraa-Teleilat, a middle PPNB site (8000–7500 calibrated BC in the review's Table 1) on the Turkish Euphrates.

evidence.supports: For the Euphrates region, the earliest large-scale reduction in size, evident as the LSI median moves below the interquartile range of the Mureybet aurochs, is at MPPNB Mezraa-Teleilat on the Turkish Euphrates dating to the early-mid eighth millennium BC

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: Helmer et al. 2005 and Bollongino et al. 2012 were not opened directly; both are known here only through the review.
The Dja'de al-Mughara coordinates are from memory and unconfirmed (the researcher found 36.38 N and 36.65 N in two places); check them against an excavation report.
Mezraa-Teleilat is given only as 'on the Turkish Euphrates' in the source, so its event is placed on the region and not on a point.
The Tigris evidence (Çayönü) and Shillourokambos, which the review also discusses, are not covered and bear on which place was first.

research.note: The review says the upper Euphrates has been presented as the hearth of taurine cattle domestication, but it disputes a single centre and cites cattle management just as early in the Tigris drainage and the southern Levant, so priority is not settled.
